title: CLO2024.2 - GPU Simulation
description: CLO2024.2 brings more powerful simulation capabilities! The new GPU simulation feature enables faster simulations with the same accuracy and collision handling capabilities as CPU simulation.
transcript:
In version 2022.4.2, we improved the conflict processing function of GPU simulation, enabling stable simulation when simulating multi-layered plate clothing. Additionally, conflict processing between the plate and the virtual model now runs smoothly, increasing work efficiency. 

Let's take a closer look at these improvements through an example.

First, let’s review the UI changes in the software interface. Since GPU simulation has been enhanced and its scope of use expanded, we have improved the simulation function menu. 

We added animation options used for recording animation, completion, and image rendering. Furthermore, a menu for setting CPU and GPU options has been added below the simulation type. It is now possible to set CPU and GPU options separately for normal, test, and animation simulations. When the GPU option is selected, simulation icons are displayed as empty keys.

Next, let’s compare GPU and CPU usage. To make a clear comparison, click on the main menu to set the display environment to "display real speed," which shows information and FPS of the current version at the bottom left of the 3D window.

First, compare the simulation speed at normal speed with the default settings—GPU on the left and CPU on the right. It is evident that GPU simulation is significantly faster in terms of speed.

Next, we will simulate using the test mode. Similarly, GPU simulation runs much faster than CPU simulation. Please note that GPU simulation speed may vary depending on the graphics card performance.

After selecting GPU simulation, you can manipulate the board in the 3D window to observe the simulation’s stability. Even with multi-layered boards, simulation remains stable.

Next, we demonstrate using GPU simulation in animation mode to record the process of simulating multi-layered plate clothing. After selecting GPU simulation, you can manipulate the board in the 3D window to check the stability. Even with multiple layers, the simulation remains stable.

When the agreed loss factor strength is relatively low and the number of boards and layers increases, GPU simulation is much faster and more stable than before. However, this may also depend on the graphics card performance.

Please note that GPU simulation currently applies only to ordinary clothing simulation and does not support wool products. Additionally, it is not applicable to secondary simulation or virtual model simulation at this time.

Besides improving simulation speed, the enhancement of conflict processing has also improved the accuracy of GPU simulation, producing results equivalent to those of CPU simulation.

Furthermore, when saving project files, ensure that the option to exclude saving the processor is not selected. For example, when saving this file, CPU is selected.

In test mode, the GPU simulation mode switches to GPU normal mode in the software, and when reopening the file, it will revert to the processor option selected at that time. However, normal test mode and animation simulation options are saved within the file and become the test mode.

With these improvements, GPU simulation can now be performed stably and quickly. We invite you to experience GPU simulation.

Thank you for your attention. Please share your feedback and suggestions in the message area.

chunks.content: ## GPU Simulation Improvements in CLO2022.4.2 This section covers enhancements in GPU simulation for CLO version 2022.4.2, focusing on conflict processing, simulation stability, UI updates, and performance comparisons between GPU and CPU simulations. In version 2022.4.2, the conflict processing function for GPU simulation was improved to enable stable simulation of multi-layered plate clothing. Conflict handling between the plate and the virtual model now runs smoothly, enhancing work efficiency and simulation accuracy. These improvements bring GPU simulation results closer to those of CPU simulation in terms of precision. ### User Interface Updates The software interface has been updated to accommodate the expanded use and improved performance of GPU simulation. Key UI changes include: - An enhanced simulation function menu reflecting GPU simulation improvements. - Added animation options for recording animation, completion, and image rendering. - A new menu for setting CPU and GPU options separately beneath the simulation type selection. - Separate CPU and GPU settings for normal, test, and animation simulations. - When GPU simulation is selected, simulation icons display as empty keys for clarity. These UI changes provide users with more control over simulation modes and hardware utilization. ## Performance Comparison Between GPU and CPU Simulation This section details the procedure and results for comparing GPU and CPU simulation speeds and stability in CLO 2022.4.2. To compare GPU and CPU performance: 1. Set the display environment to “display real speed” via the main menu. This shows current FPS and version info at the bottom left of the 3D window. 2. Run normal speed simulations with default settings, observing GPU simulation on the left and CPU simulation on the right. Results show: - GPU simulation is significantly faster than CPU simulation under normal mode. - In test mode, GPU simulation maintains much faster speeds compared to CPU simulation. - Simulation speed on GPU varies depending on the graphics card performance. Users can manipulate multi-layered boards in the 3D window during GPU simulation to verify stability, which remains consistent even with multiple layers. ## GPU Simulation for Animation Mode and Stability This section explains the use of GPU simulation in animation mode and its stability when simulating multi-layered plate clothing. When selecting GPU simulation in animation mode: - Users can record the entire simulation process. - Manipulation of the board within the 3D window confirms that simulation remains stable across multiple layers. - Stability and speed improve especially when the agreed loss factor strength is relatively low and the number of boards and layers increases. However, GPU simulation performance and stability are dependent on the quality of the graphics card. ## Current Limitations and Compatibility This section highlights current restrictions and compatibility notes for GPU simulation in CLO 2022.4.2. - GPU simulation applies only to ordinary clothing simulation. - It does *not* support wool products. - GPU simulation is not applicable for secondary simulations or virtual model simulations at this time. - For accurate GPU simulation results, project files must be saved without excluding the processor option.

For example, when saving, ensure CPU is selected if applicable. - In test mode, GPU simulation switches to GPU normal mode in the software; upon reopening the file, it reverts to the processor option selected during saving. - Normal test mode and animation simulation options are preserved within the project file and restore test mode status. ## Summary With these enhancements, CLO 2022.4.2 enables faster and more stable GPU simulation of multi-layered plate clothing, improved conflict processing, and a more user-friendly interface with separate CPU/GPU settings for different simulation modes.
